panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (Left-a, Left-b, Right-a, Right-b). Left-a: Greyscale ultrasound of left testis in adolescent with concurrent mumps parotitis, pancreatitis and orchitis per article title; caption and in-text describe swelling with heterogenous hypoechogenicity of testis. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: T1WI axial parotid MRI from iodide mumps case with in-text bilateral parotid enlargement; panel visibly shows enlarged parotid glands. B: T2WI axial parotid MRI from iodide mumps case; visibly shows bilateral parotid swelling corresponding to described enlargement. C: T2WI coronal view showing swollen parotid regions in same patient with stated bilateral parotid enlargement. D: DWI axial image of same enlarged parotids; low-resolution but shows parotid swelling contours in disease context. E: ADC map of same enlarged parotids; shows parotid swelling contours in iodide mumps case.
panels.attribution_text: Zhang et al. The pathogenesis of iodide mumps: A case report.. Medicine 2017. doi:10.1097/md.0000000000008881. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Parotid MRI and DWI. Representative MRI images showing the T1WI axial (A), T2WI axial (B), and T2WI coronal views (C). DWI (D) and ADC (E) images. ADC = apparent diffusion coefficient, DWI = diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging, MRI = magnetic resonance imaging.
in_text_mentions: mination showed bilateral parotid area enlargement centred on the earlobe; the left side was 3′4 cm large, the right side was 3′3 cm large, and the masses were moderately firm with no obvious fluctuation and without vascular murmur (Fig. 1A and B). Bilateral parotid ultrasound showed a diffuse enlargement of the glands with a homogeneous echo. DWI indicated no obvious limited diffusion (Fig. 2). Intravenous dexamethasone (5 mg) was administered 20 hours post-DSA, after which the bilateral parotid shrunk (Fig. 1C). By 4 days postsurgery, the patient's bilateral parotid had recovered completely.

plate_findings.evidence: swelling of the left parotid and submandibular glands

panels.body_site: neck - left parotid and submandibular glands
panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Panel-specific caption plus in-text describe swelling of left parotid/submandibular glands in anesthesia mumps case report; title is mumps-focused. CT visibly shows enlarged gland with edema consistent with parotid swelling manifestation. b: MRI confirms inflammatory process of the parotid and submandibular glands with swelling in same anesthesia mumps patient; T1 fat-suppressed scan visibly shows enlarged gland, supporting mumps parotid swelling attribution.
panels.attribution_text: Cavaliere et al. Massive facial edema and airway obstruction secondary to acute postoperative sialadenitis or "anesthesia mumps": a case report.. Journal of medical case reports 2009. doi:10.1186/1752-1947-3-7073. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Enhanced computed tomography (a; 7 hours after the end of surgery) and T1 fat-suppressed magnetic resonance (b; 3rd postoperative day) axial scans of the neck. The left submandibular gland (arrows) is enlarged, with increased vascularization. The lobular architecture of the gland is conserved and no salivary stones or ductal dilations are evident. A phlegmon is present in the left submandibular space, with obliteration of the fat planes and involvement of the subcutaneous fat. The larynx and trachea are compressed around the tracheal tube (arrowheads) and dislocated to the right side.
in_text_mentions: avenously TID; and clindamycin, 600 mg intravenously TID). During the night, serum amylases rose to 230 IU/L and contrast enhanced spiral computed tomography of the head and neck performed 7 hours after the end of surgery showed swelling of the left parotid and submandibular glands with a marked edema that spread to the periglandular fat, muscles, and aponeuroses. Glandular ducts were not dilated and no calculus was observed. Both larynx and pharynx were markedly edematous and the airway lumen was totally obliterated so that no empty space was observed around the endotracheal tube (Figure 1a).

On the 3rd postoperative day, magnetic resonance imaging of the head and neck was performed with intravenous contrast enhancement (Figure 1b). The exam confirmed the inflammatory process of the parotid and submandibular glands, showing swelling, areas of inhomogeneous signal, and marked enhancement after intravenous contrast. Edema and increased contrast enhancement were also observed in the superficial and deep neck spaces, particularly in the masticatory space. The tongue base was still enlarged and the pharynx and larynx were dislocated to the right.
